# OUTARCH

> One command center for your terminals, dev servers, tests, and AI coding agents on Windows.

## Overview

OUTARCH is a developer workstation application designed for Windows 11. It organizes command-line tasks, long-running processes (dev servers, test watchers, databases), and autonomous AI coding agents into a supervised workspace. When an agent or task encounters an error, finishes a job, or requests user confirmation, OUTARCH alerts the developer so they can intervene promptly without constantly switching windows.

- **Website**: https://outarch.com
- **Operating System**: Windows 11 (requires Node.js 22 LTS)
- **Architecture**: Local-first execution; code and terminals remain on the user's computer.

## Key Features

- **Multi-Terminal Supervision**: Run dev servers, test runners, build tools, and AI agents side by side in a structured grid.
- **Attention Queue ("Needs You")**: Centralized inbox that surfaces processes requiring user input, such as agent permission prompts, failed test suites, or completed recipes.
- **AI Agent Integration**: Works with any CLI-based coding agent without proxying or modifying terminal behavior. Supported agents include Claude Code, OpenAI Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Goose, and Aider.
- **Project Memory (`arch_memory.md`)**: Structured Markdown file stored in the repository to provide context and history across multiple agent sessions and manual coding workflows.
- **Mobile Companion**: Local web application that pairs over the local Wi-Fi network to monitor process statuses, view output summaries, and run saved recipes from a phone without routing through cloud servers.
- **VS Code Bridge**: Extension bridging editor diagnostics and terminal status to OUTARCH locally.

## Privacy & Data Handling

- Terminal output, files, and project operations execute locally on the user's machine.
- No terminal relay through remote servers.
- When using Mission AI assistant features, context is sent directly to the selected model provider; secret files and tokens are excluded by default.
